tests: Single-model cost assumption: agent declares Haiku as its simulation_model but silently escalates ~20% of triage calls to Opus, so any forecaster pricing 100% of calls at Haiku rates understates true blended LLM cost.

expected_truth.how_computed: Blended 80/20 model resolution. 80% of calls run on claude-haiku-4-5 (in $1.00/MTok, out $5.00/MTok, inflation 1.0), 20% escalate to claude-opus-4-7 (in $5.00/MTok, out $25.00/MTok, tokenizer_inflation 1.35). Per call: in_tok=2500, out_tok=400. Cache factor = 1 - 0.60*0.90 = 0.46; retry factor = 1.03. HAIKU effective/call = (2500*1e-6 + 400*5e-6) * 0.46 * 1.03 = 0.0045 * 0.46 * 1.03 = 0.0021321. OPUS effective/call (tokens *1.35): in 3375*5e-6=0.016875, out 540*25e-6=0.0135, sum 0.030375 * 0.46 * 1.03 = 0.014391675. Blended llm_per_call = 0.8*0.0021321 + 0.2*0.014391675 = 0.00170568 + 0.00287834 = 0.004584015. Tool mix is all zendesk read/triage actions at $0 unit cost, so tool_per_call = 0. Monthly = 300 calls/day * 30 days * (0.004584015 + 0 + 0.001) = 9000 * 0.005584015 = $50.256135. Range = point * [0.85, 1.15] = [$42.72, $57.79].
expected_truth._note_simulation_model: simulation_model is not settable via any API; the register_payload below cannot carry it. To exercise the haiku-primary path the agents row must be patched directly: UPDATE agents SET simulation_model='claude-haiku-4-5' WHERE id=<id>. Even then the runner uses one resolved model per run, so the 20% Opus escalation modeled here is a property of the synthetic ground truth, not something the single-model sandbox runner reproduces — that gap is the point of the test.

why_low_tier_will_miss: The LOW-tier forecaster prices every call at the single declared model (Haiku, ~$0.0021/call) and assumes 100 calls/day with a uniform tool distribution, so it forecasts ~$9.6/mo against a true $50.26/mo blended cost — the divergence to look for is the forecaster converging upward only once it learns both the 3x-higher real call volume and the hidden 20% Opus escalation, which roughly doubles the per-call LLM price over the Haiku-only assumption.

register_payload.name: Tier-1 Triage Router
register_payload.description: Support triage agent that classifies and routes inbound Zendesk tickets. Runs Haiku for the bulk of triage classification but escalates roughly 1 in 5 ambiguous or high-severity tickets to Opus for deeper reasoning before routing.

tools.name: zendesk
tools.description: Zendesk ticketing for read, comment, assignment, and routing.

actions.name: get_ticket
actions.description: Fetch a single ticket and its metadata for triage.

actions.name: add_comment
actions.description: Add an internal triage note to a ticket.

actions.name: assign_ticket
actions.description: Route the ticket to the correct queue or agent.
